study_name.notes: No formal study name provided; referenced as Danish AN cohort study

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.

country.evidence_quote: Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

body_site.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples

dna_extraction_kit.evidence_quote: Microbial DNAs were isolated and purified from stool samples using NucleoSpin soil mini kit
dna_extraction_kit.notes: For mouse experiments; human samples used IHMS SOP P7 V2

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer
sequencing_platform.notes: For human metagenomics; mouse 16S used Illumina MiSeq

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

sex.evidence_quote: we decided to include only women in the present study
sex.notes: Study includes only females; approximately 95% of AN cases are women

age_group.evidence_quote: EDI-3 was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years
age_group.notes: Inferred from age range in study; specific participant ages not provided in aggregate

control.notes: Sample-level designation requires per-participant data; cohort includes both AN cases and healthy controls but individual assignment not provided

subject_id.notes: No individual participant IDs provided in paper; cohort of 77 AN cases and 70 controls aggregated

sample_id.notes: No individual sample IDs provided; data presented at cohort level

age_years.notes: Age-matched control women mentioned but specific ages not provided for human cohort. FMT donors: AN cases aged 20, 22, 20 yr; HC cases aged 20, 22, 21 yr.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion applied to both AN and HC groups

bmi.notes: FMT donors: AN cases BMI 10.3, 11.5, 11.7 kg/m²; HC cases BMI 22.6, 21.1, 21.2 kg/m². General population data: HC exclusion criterion BMI below 18.5 or above 25 kg/m².

disease.evidence_quote: AN patients were all diagnosed by an experienced consultant psychiatrist and they met the DSM-5 criteria
disease.notes: Study includes 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females

disease_details.evidence_quote: It can be classified into two subtypes, the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: AN-RS n=56, AN-BP n=21 in human cohort

fmt_role.evidence_quote: faecal microbiota from three randomly chosen AN-RS cases and three age-matched HC participants to three independent litters of female germ-free (GF) mice
fmt_role.section: Results — Gut microbiota induces reduced weight gain
fmt_role.notes: FMT mice were germ-free recipients after colonization with human donor material

treatment.evidence_quote: All the included patients were treated in specialized centres. Care was given by a multidisciplinary team
treatment.notes: Medications and treatments specified as covariates in deconfounding analyses for AN cases

smoker.evidence_quote: smoking and multiple drug intake were defined as covariates
smoker.notes: Smoking history used as a covariate in statistical models but specific smoking status for each group not reported

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Multiple bacterial taxa (for example, Clostridium species) were altered in AN and correlated with estimates of eating behaviour
biomarker_name.notes: Biomarkers identified across multiple sections including Abstract, Results, and Methods. List includes bacterial taxa, viral species, metabolites, and clinical chemistry measures reported as altered in AN versus controls.

biomarker_unit.notes: Units for biomarker values are not reported in the paper. Most measurements are relative abundance or presence/absence data from metagenomics.

value: inversely correlated with eating disorder scores
inversely correlated with eating disorder scores
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Clostridium species were positively correlated with eating disorder scores
biomarker_value.notes: Biomarker values represent directional changes (higher/lower/depleted) or associations with eating disorder measures in AN compared to healthy controls.

disease_response_os.notes: Anorexia nervosa is not presented as a fatal disease with mortality tracking in this study. The paper mentions population mortality rate of 5.6% per decade but does not report individual survival data.

disease_response_os_unit.notes: No overall survival data reported for study participants.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status is not a relevant measure for anorexia nervosa and was not reported in this study.

value: reduced bacterial cell counts in AN not significant
higher β-diversity at species level in AN
reduced viral-bacterial interactions in AN (219 HC vs 84 AN)
31 viral species enriched or decreased in AN
25 of 30 increased viral species were Lactococcus phages
5056 deletion structural variants and 2423 variable SVs identified
predicted bacterial growth rates reduced in 6 species in AN
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Comparing stool samples from AN and HC, there was no significant difference in bacterial cell counts
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal phenotypes include microbiota composition, diversity metrics, viral communities, and structural variants measured via shotgun metagenomics.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Anorexia nervosa is not a malignancy; tumor measurements are not applicable.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable to anorexia nervosa research.

value: 77 female AN cases and 70 age-matched healthy control females
Cohort: Danish Caucasian women, recruited from 3 specialized centers
AN subtypes: 56 restricting type (AN-RS), 21 binge-eating/purging type (AN-BP)
FMT experiment: germ-free mice received fecal microbiota from AN or HC donors
Energy-restricted diet in mice: 30% calorie restriction for 3 weeks
Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics performed on fecal and serum samples
EDI-3 questionnaire used to assess eating behavior
Bidirectional mediation analyses performed to infer causal relationships
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females
uncurated_metadata.notes: Additional study design, demographic, and procedural details extracted from Methods and Results sections.

host_species.evidence_quote: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females... germ-free mice... transplanted faecal microbiota
host_species.notes: Study included both human participants (females) and experimental germ-free mice (female Swiss Webster strain).

extraction_warnings: Granularity set to sample_level per schema, but paper provides only study-level and subgroup-level (AN vs. HC, AN-RS vs. AN-BP) aggregated data. No per-sample rows with individual subject/sample IDs are available in the main text or supplementary tables.
Sample-level fields (subject_id, sample_id, control assignment) cannot be extracted because the paper does not provide individual participant identifiers or per-sample metadata tables.
Age is reported only for the human donor mice subgroup in the FMT experiment (ages 20, 20, 22 yr for AN donors; 20, 21, 22 yr for HC donors) and not for the main human cohort.
The study included both inpatient and outpatient AN cases with distinct characteristics, but individual classification not provided per participant.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Batch 1 subgroups ['AN (Anorexia Nervosa) cases', 'HC (Healthy Controls)', 'AN-RS (Anorexia Nervosa - Restricting subtype)', 'AN-BP (Anorexia Nervosa - Binge/Purging subtype)', 'FMT AN-T (Fecal Microbiota Transplant - AN donor recipients)', 'FMT HC-T (Fecal Microbiota Transplant - HC donor recipients)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.

Age information for human cohort (AN cases and HC) is stated as 'age-matched' but specific mean age or age range not provided in main text or supplementary tables accessible in the provided paper section.

Individual BMI values for human AN and HC cohorts are not provided; only FMT donor-specific BMI values (3 AN cases: 10.3, 11.5, 11.7; 3 HC cases: 22.6, 21.1, 21.2) and HC exclusion criterion (BMI 18.5-25) are stated.
Smoking status details (current/former/never) not specified for study groups; only used as statistical covariate.

Treatment details for HC group not applicable; AN group received multidisciplinary treatment at specialized centers with medications (SSRIs, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines) as specified covariates but individual treatment assignment not provided.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

The schema appears designed for oncology studies (ECOG, tumor size, OS). Anorexia nervosa is a psychiatric/metabolic condition with different clinical endpoints. Only host_species and uncurated_metadata fields are directly applicable.

Biomarker values are primarily directional (higher/lower in AN) rather than absolute measurements. Most are relative abundance measurements from shotgun metagenomics without specific numeric thresholds.
FMT mouse experiments represent mechanistic studies but not traditional disease response endpoints like survival or remission rate.
The paper reports multiple subgroups (AN-RS vs AN-BP, in-patients vs out-patients) but the schema lacks subgroup_level granularity fields appropriate to eating disorder outcomes.
Biomarker units are rarely specified; most measures are relative abundances from metagenomics or metabolomics profiling.
